newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien urges CAW members vote on Canadian.
newsitem.headline: Chretien urges CAW members vote on Canadian.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien urged the Canadian Auto Workers on Thursday to follow a government order and allow its members to vote on a restructuring plan for Canadian Airlines Corp.

Chretien said that in ordering the free vote by members, the federal government was not taking sides in the negotiations between the airline and the CAW, which represents 3,700 of the carrier's sales and ticket agents.
"We want everyone to have the chance to express themselves," Chretien told reporters after a speech.

"Everybody has participated to try to find a solution. Three levels of governments, four more unions and American Airlines ... and the members of a union that wanted to vote, because it's their future" Chretien said.
Chretien said there was no possibility of financial aid from the government for Canadian Airlines.
"What is on the table, it's on the table. It's for the participants to decide," Chretien said.
On Wednesday, Canada's labor minister invoked an obscure section of Canada's labor laws to force the free vote by the CAW members on the restructuring package.

CAW president Buzz Hargrove is opposed to the restructuring package, which calls for wage rollbacks for the 3,700 sales and ticket agents. But Hargrove said earlier Thursday that the union executive has little choice but to allow the vote.
